questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to become a zookeeper
Why pandas are disappearing
The most popular zoos in the world
The arguments for and against keeping animals in zoos
questions.why: They debate the pros and cons of keeping animals in zoos.

questions.q: What is Neil's opinion of zoos at the start?
options: He thinks they should all close because keeping animals locked up is cruel
He sees good reasons for them but also finds them a bit sad
He loves visiting them
He has never thought about it
questions.why: He says there are good scientific reasons, but it seems 'a little bit sad and cruel'.

questions.q: How many people visit zoos every year?
options: Around 700 million
Around 70 million
Around 7 billion
Around 17 million people
questions.why: Georgie mentions an estimated 700 million visitors every year.

questions.q: According to reporter William Lee Adams, what is the main reason zoos give for existing?
options: Making money for cities
Giving animals medical care
Education
Entertainment for families
questions.why: He says education is the primary reason zoos give for why they should exist.

questions.q: Why does William mention his visits to Zoo Atlanta as a child?
options: To say that lowland gorillas have always been his favourite animal
To complain that the trips were boring
To show how school trips introduce children to conservation
To explain why he became a reporter
questions.why: He saw the gorillas every year, and 'the point of this was to introduce us to conservation'.

questions.q: Why does William talk about pandas?
options: Because they often escape from zoos
Because they are the most popular animal with visitors in every zoo
Because they are dangerous to visitors
Because zoos spend money on research to help them breed
questions.why: He says pandas are reluctant to mate and a lot of zoo money goes to encouraging them.

questions.q: What are animal-rights activist Nikita Dhawan's reasons against zoos?
options: Zoos are too expensive to visit
Zoos harm animals' health and can't copy their natural homes
Zoos teach children the wrong facts about how wild animals live
Zoos don't have enough visitors
questions.why: She mentions harm to animals' physical and psychological health and says zoos can't mimic natural habitats.

questions.q: Has Neil changed his opinion by the end?
options: No, he still isn't sure because both sides are strong
Yes, after hearing Nikita he now thinks all zoos are cruel
Yes, he now fully supports zoos
He refuses to give an opinion
questions.why: Neil says there are strong arguments on both sides, 'so I'm still not sure'.
